title: Chicken or Turkey a la King with Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey a la King is tender poultry simmered in a light broth‑based sauce with aromatic vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens). The sauce contains no cream, dairy, potatoes, or soup base, making the dish lighter and suitable for diets limiting dairy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The "a la King" dish originated in the United States in the early 1900s and quickly spread to Europe.
The classic recipe includes mushrooms, but the vegetable‑only version uses a clear broth, preserving a delicate flavor.
Adding broccoli and leafy greens boosts the content of vitamins B‑complex and C.
Both chicken and turkey stay juicy because they are quickly braised in the sauce rather than roasted.

items.title: Rich source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Omitting cream and dairy reduces saturated fat compared with the traditional version.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Carrots supply beta‑carotene, broccoli adds vitamin K and folate, and leafy greens contribute iron and vitamin C.

items.title: Immune‑supporting nutrients
items.content: Vitamin C from greens and beta‑carotene from carrots help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The absence of starchy ingredients (potatoes, cream) makes the dish suitable for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or turkey; discontinue use if symptoms appear.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using store‑bought broth can raise sodium levels; opt for low‑sodium broth when possible.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large broccoli florets may cause discomfort for sensitive stomachs; chop finely.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté bite‑size pieces of chicken or turkey until lightly browned, then add diced carrots, broccoli florets, and chopped leafy greens. Pour in vegetable broth, cover, and simmer 15‑20 minutes until vegetables are tender. For a slightly thicker sauce, stir in a small amount of cornstarch mixed with cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth to keep the sauce from drying out.
